superseded.detail: Superseded, not rewritten: these measurements remain evidence for the exact comparator versions recorded above. The installed comparators have moved, so a fresh runset is required before treating the measurements as current.

title: S2 comparative baseline: like-for-like on wrapping AND pinning, reported by frame tick

replication.note: Run 20 minutes earlier on the same machine and window, before 8 commits landed. Retained because comparing the two is what exposed the headline finding — not as a second baseline.

repeats: 7 per adapter per runset; 14 per adapter pooled

supersedes.status/milestones/2026-08-15-s2-comparat: That runset honoured S2's `pinned_left: 1` in pretable only. #413 added it to ag-grid and tanstack.
supersedes.note: It also reported single medians per adapter. Finding F1 below is that those medians were not reproducible statistics for three of the four grids.

headline: Three of the four grids do not have a stable frame cost on S2 scroll — they oscillate between adjacent 120Hz tick counts, so their MEDIAN is an artifact of which repeats landed where. pretable is the only one that holds a single tick. Report the tick distribution, not the median.

frameTickDistribution.note: scroll_frame_p95_ms is frame-quantised: 8.3 / 16.7 / 25.0 / 33.3 / 41.7 / 50.0ms are 1-6 ticks of a 120Hz frame. Each repeat's p95 snaps to one of these. 14 repeats per adapter, pooled across both runsets.

medians.warning: Recorded for continuity with earlier milestones. For every adapter except pretable these are sampling artifacts — see F1 — and should not be quoted as point estimates or differenced against each other.

structural.note: sd 0.00 for every adapter on every one of these, in both runsets. These are the load-insensitive numbers and they are safe to quote.

environmentFitness.verdict: Fit. The strongest evidence is internal to the data rather than external to it.
environmentFitness.control: pretable returned sd 0.29 and 0.31 in the two runsets, and 14/14 repeats at the same tick. A machine distorting frame timing cannot leave one adapter's tail untouched across 14 runs while moving three others.
environmentFitness.structural: Every structural metric returned sd 0.00 for all four adapters in both runsets.
environmentFitness.mui_as_second_control: MUI's code did not change between the two runsets and its median moved 32.1 -> 32.0. The machine was the same in both.
environmentFitness.machine: 10 logical cores, freshly restarted, 0 bytes swap, no concurrent agent sessions — the user paused them deliberately for this window. idle 78.4% before / 74.3% after the primary run.
environmentFitness.howThisWindowWasFound: Two automated watches (8h daytime, 11h overnight) never opened a gate; this machine normally hosts several concurrent agent sessions and sat below 8% idle throughout. It took a deliberate restart.
gateDesignNotes: Gating on process NAMES (playwright/vite/bench) is wrong: it reported busy=0 while six `zsh` processes from other agent sessions held the machine at 0.98% idle.

Gating on the busiest process is also wrong: WindowServer sits at ~48% compositing the Claude desktop app that runs the session, and the previous baseline was measured under exactly that condition. A threshold stricter than the baseline's own conditions can never open.
`ps aux` %CPU is a LIFETIME AVERAGE, not instantaneous. Use `top -l 2` and take the SECOND sample; the first reports since boot.

findings.title: Medians are not reproducible for three of the four grids
findings.detail: TanStack's median moved 17.6 -> 25.0 between two runsets 20 minutes apart on the same machine with no change to its adapter. Nothing regressed: its repeats are bimodal at 2 and 3 ticks (17.5/17.6/17.5/17.4/25.0/24.9/25.2 then 25.8/25.0/25.1/25.1/18.3/25.0/23.8), so the median simply reports which side won that sample. ag-grid is bimodal at 5 and 6 ticks, MUI at 3 and 4. Any comparison that differences these medians — including a `p95 X vs Y` table — is measuring the draw, not the library.

findings.title: pretable is the only grid with a stable frame cost
findings.detail: 14/14 repeats at 2 ticks across both runsets, sd 0.29 and 0.31. The other three each straddle two tick values. This is the strongest claim in the file and it is a claim about CONSISTENCY, not speed: a median can be argued about across machines, but one adapter holding a single tick for 14 runs while three others oscillate in the same window cannot be explained by the machine.

findings.title: The earlier 'ag-grid got faster while doing more work' puzzle was sampling
findings.detail: The 2026-08-15 milestone recorded ag-grid at 48.3 and this run reads 41.7-43.1, which looked like it improved after gaining a pinned zone. It did not. ag-grid draws from {41.7, 50.0} and the earlier sample happened to include more 50.0s (its sd was 7.92). The +54 DOM nodes (596 -> 650) are the real, load-insensitive evidence that the pinned container is being rendered.

findings.title: TanStack's pinning cost is a shift in the tick MIX, not a shift in median
findings.detail: Before pinning (2026-08-15) TanStack was sd 0.39 — effectively always 2 ticks. After pinning it draws 5/14 at 2 ticks and 9/14 at 3. Its DOM is unchanged at 704 because sticky positioning adds no nodes, so the whole cost lands in per-frame compositing. The honest statement is that pinning moved TanStack from reliably-2-ticks to mostly-3-ticks, which a median comparison of 17.6 vs 17.6 would have called free.

findings.title: TanStack's 592px scroll-anchor shift is unchanged by pinning
findings.detail: scroll_anchor_shift_forward_p95_px is 592 for TanStack and 0 for the other three, identical across all three runsets to date. It is sd 0.00 — a structural count, not a timing — so unlike the frame numbers it is quotable as-is. It remains the one metric where the two grids are not close.

findings.title: The DOM comparison is column virtualization, not per-cell leanness
findings.detail: Repeated from the superseded file because it is the easiest number to misquote: pretable draws 72 rendered cells to TanStack's 640 and MUI's 943 (6 per row against ~40) because it and ag-grid virtualize columns. Per rendered CELL pretable is 1.88 nodes against TanStack's 1.10. A nodes-per-ROW reading inverts the ranking.

findings.title: MUI cannot pin at all
findings.detail: Column pinning is an MUI X Pro feature; the matrix runs Community. Verified against the installed 9.11.0 — no `pinnedColumns` prop, no `pinned` on GridColDef, no `columnPinning` under hooks/features/. MUI is measured WITHOUT a pinned zone while the other three have one, permanently. The capability gap is itself a comparative finding.
